sentiment.instructions: Judge the sentiment the tweet's author conveys, either their own feeling or the clearly good or bad nature of what they report. Topic words (dates, names, 'may', ordinals) do not count, and neither do exclamation marks or 'lol' on their own. When there is no clear positive or negative leaning, choose neutral.

criteria.positive: Explicit positive feeling: excitement ('can't wait', 'fast forward to', 'celebrate', 'perfect night', 'for sure going'), love, praise, pride, gratitude, hope, or warm wishes and prayers. Also the author inviting people to join their own event or outing ('come with us', 'come support', 'let's go'), or happily indulging in a favorite thing. Also reports of completed good outcomes: a win, title, record, history made, someone delighted. Also promotions offering appealing tickets, prizes, free items or hype ('don't miss').
criteria.neutral: Bare plans and logistics with no stated enthusiasm, plain event listings, info sessions and sign-ups. Also questions, requests, fan pleas, trivia, jokes, memes, spam and incoherent text. Also in-progress game updates, speculative headlines ('may'), mild comparisons of politicians or players, and wire-style celebrity news such as births and birthdays. Also wry commentary. Also lighthearted self-deprecation or mock gripes ('lol', 'lmao', 'I'm dead', 'not ready').
criteria.negative: Frustration, anger, disappointment, sadness, fear, insult or criticism ('sucks', 'disappointed', 'hate', 'shameful', 'NOOO' at news, 'miss'). Short grumbles or digs also count ('don't know why they haven't...', mocking a day or a person, 'no talent'), as do pointed arguments against someone's view. Also reports of harmful events: attacks, missiles, deaths and funerals, crimes and arrests, crashes, deficits, devices breaking, conflict.
